articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:09:21 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
Disappointment (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Disappointment' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others ‌were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and ‌travel, Emtedad website quoted lawyer ‌Mostafa ⁠Nili as saying

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An Iranian singer and four members of her production ​team have each received 74 lashes after being ‌sentenced for "offending public decency by ​producing and publishing obscene and ⁠immoral content online", an Iranian news website said on Monday (November 23, 2026). Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others ‌were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and ‌travel, the Emtedad website quoted lawyer ‌Mostafa ⁠Nili as saying. The case ⁠followed the release of a video on YouTube in December 2024 showing Ms. Ahmadi performing without the ​mandatory hijab alongside male ‌musicians in Qom, south of the capital Tehran, Norway-based human rights group Hengaw said. Western governments and human rights ‌groups have criticised flogging as torture ​and a violation of international law. Iran rejects accusations over its ⁠human rights record, saying Western countries should focus on their own human rights ‌problems. Iranian authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment by Reuters. Rules requiring women to wear the hijab were a flashpoint during protests in 2022 after the death ‌in custody of Kurdish Iranian woman Mahsa Amini, ​who was arrested for allegedly violating the dress code. The rules have increasingly ⁠been flouted on the streets of Tehran ⁠and beyond, and enforcement of the rules has also become more ‌selective.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Emtedad did not specify whether Mr. Nili had represented the five defendants.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs: Humaiun Kobir
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. • 1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. Ms. Hasina has urged Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesman said. Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance." "A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The chants were familiar. But this time, they echoed not in Tehran, but in Herat. In mid-June, Afghanistan’s western city of Herat witnessed a rare display of public defiance against the Taliban. Women, and this time, men too, marched through the streets chanting “Women, Work and Freedom”, a slogan probably inspired by Iran’s 2022 “Woman, Life and Freedom” movement that emerged after the death of the 22-year-old Mahsa Amini. According to Zan Times , an exiled media organisation run by Afghan women journalists, the latest crackdown appears to have been planned days in advance. On June 4, Herat’s governor Noor Ahmad Islamjar reportedly met with a group of morality enforcers. On the afternoon of June 5, Taliban officials used the end of Friday prayers to announce that women who failed to comply with the Islamic dress code would be arrested. The following morning, the arrests began.

articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began? With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him. Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities. While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto! One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery. Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs. The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement “The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 What do lemurs and opera singers share?

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:10:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began? With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him. Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities. While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto! One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery. Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs. The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement “The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Conversation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conversation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Conservation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "What do lemurs and opera singers share?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back." (Hinglish Arth: हाल ही में, एक अध्ययन से पता चला है कि इंद्री लेमर्स उसी पद्धति का उपयोग करते हैं जो ओपेरा गायक यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए करते हैं कि उनकी आवाज़ पीछे बैठे दर्शकों तक पहुंचे।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "What do lemurs and opera singers share?"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t." (Hinglish Arth: घने जंगल में संचार करने वाले एक जानवर के लिए, यह उस गीत के बीच अंतर कर सकता है जो प्रसारित होता है और जो नहीं करता है।)

articles.title: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO: 6 CEOs who reclaimed their top positions
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, 2026.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Jensen Huang, co-founder of Nvidia, who had stepped down as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the chipmaker, was re-instated in the top job on November 23, 2026. Mr Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, and CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO. The board voted unanimously to bring Mr Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, Nvidia said in a statement. Huang’s return has put the spotlight on the ouster and return of other top bosses. Here’s a look at some of the major names. Former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The return of Mr Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia is unique, as reports suggest that senior U.S. government officials left the company’s board confident that he posed no national security risk amid concerns of China vying for the company’s advanced chips. U.S. President Donald Trump also welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” I believe my ​intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back,” Mr Trump told CNBC after Mr Huang’s reinstatement, marking an unprecedented intervention by U.S. government officials into the matters of a publicly traded company.

Mr Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, and CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO. The board voted unanimously to bring Mr Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, Nvidia said in a statement. Huang’s return has put the spotlight on the ouster and return of other top bosses. Here’s a look at some of the major names. Former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena

U.S. President Donald Trump also welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” I believe my ​intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back,” Mr Trump told CNBC after Mr Huang’s reinstatement, marking an unprecedented intervention by U.S. government officials into the matters of a publicly traded company.

articles.title: Webinar on autoimmune conditions to be held on November 28
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The webinar will examine how autoimmune conditions develop, their common symptoms, the challenges in diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and long-term management

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms. The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention. The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options. The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations. The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To register, click here or scan the QR code given below.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Webinar on autoimmune conditions to be held on November 28

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 04:32:15 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The webinar will examine how autoimmune conditions develop, their common symptoms, the challenges in diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and long-term management

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms. The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention. The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options. The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations. The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To register, click here or scan the QR code given below.

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms. The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention. The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options. The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations. The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: After a successful organ transport in August for the first time, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has once again facilitated the movement of a human organ. On September 11, a live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital. According to BMRCL, the transport operation commenced at 11.01 p.m. and concluded at 11.21 p.m. covering seven stations in just 20 minutes. The BMRCL stated that the heart was carried inside Train ID 12, Train Set 29, accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. To ensure smooth movement, the Assistant Security Officer coordinated with the Sparsh team and metro security personnel, making special arrangements to avoid delays and provide a safe corridor for the critical transfer. Bengaluru Metro facilitates transportation of donor heart from Goraguntepalya to Bommasandra A live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital on September 11, 2025. The organ was accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ. A donated human liver, meant for transplantation, was transported from Vydehi Hospital at Whitefield to Sparsh Hospital at R.R. Nagar. The operation was executed using a combination of ambulance and metro, significantly reducing travel time during peak traffic hours. After its first organ transport in August, #Bengaluru 's Namma Metro again facilitated an organ transport on Sept 11. A live human heart was moved from Yeshwanthpur to South End Circle in just 20 minutes for a transplant at Apollo Hospital. @the_hindu @THBengaluru pic.twitter.com/g3ZrWNMZ7M
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bengaluru / public transport / health / medical service

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Bengaluru metro facilitates organ transport for second time

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 04:16:45 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: After a successful organ transport in August for the first time, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has once again facilitated the movement of a human organ. On September 11, a live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital. According to BMRCL, the transport operation commenced at 11.01 p.m. and concluded at 11.21 p.m. covering seven stations in just 20 minutes. The BMRCL stated that the heart was carried inside Train ID 12, Train Set 29, accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. To ensure smooth movement, the Assistant Security Officer coordinated with the Sparsh team and metro security personnel, making special arrangements to avoid delays and provide a safe corridor for the critical transfer. Bengaluru Metro facilitates transportation of donor heart from Goraguntepalya to Bommasandra A live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital on September 11, 2025. The organ was accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ. A donated human liver, meant for transplantation, was transported from Vydehi Hospital at Whitefield to Sparsh Hospital at R.R. Nagar. The operation was executed using a combination of ambulance and metro, significantly reducing travel time during peak traffic hours. After its first organ transport in August, #Bengaluru 's Namma Metro again facilitated an organ transport on Sept 11. articles.title: De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges. Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk. The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules. Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

hinglishTracks.en: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

hinglishTracks.en: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — राष्ट्रीय चिकित्सा आयोग (एनएमसी) ने चिकित्सा शिक्षा मानकों के रखरखाव विनियम, 2023 (एमएसएमईआर-2023) को गैर-अधिसूचित और वापस ले लिया है, जहां मेडिकल कॉलेजों में शैक्षिक मानकों और बुनियादी ढांचे की आवश्यकताओं के उल्लंघन के लिए मेडिकल कॉलेजों को दंड जुर्माना का सामना करना पड़ता था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — द हिंदू की पहले की रिपोर्टों में कहा गया था कि एनएमसी द्वारा एमएसएमईआर-2023 को वापस लेने से गलत जानकारी प्रस्तुत करने के लिए व्यक्तिगत संकाय सदस्यों और प्रशासकों पर ₹5 लाख तक का जुर्माना लगाने के प्रावधानों को हटाकर चिकित्सा शिक्षा में जवाबदेही कमजोर हो गई है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Accountability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability और Antonyms हैं: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility।

hinglishTracks.en: Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — हालाँकि मेडिकल असेसमेंट एंड रेटिंग बोर्ड (MARB) अभी भी अलग-अलग नियमों के तहत संस्थानों को ₹1 करोड़ तक का जुर्माना लगा सकता है, लेकिन व्यक्तिगत कदाचार को रोकने में संस्थागत दंड कम प्रभावी हो सकते हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 03:52:50 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges. Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk. The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules. Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Relaxation (Noun)
नियमों में ढील या छूट — किसी कड़े प्रतिबंध को थोड़े समय के लिए हल्का करना।
✓ Syn: Moderation, Easing, Leniency  |  ✖ Ant: Strictness, Tightening, Rigidity
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlappin' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlap' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlap' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a..." (Hinglish Arth: एमएसएमईआर-2023 के तहत, एक परिभाषित वृद्धि पथ था; अब, कार्रवाई एमएआरबी आकलन शुरू करने, पूरा करने और उचित समय सीमा के भीतर कार्रवाई करने पर निर्भर करती है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping..." (Hinglish Arth: द हिंदू से बात करते हुए, एनएमसी अधिकारियों ने कहा कि डिनोटिफिकेशन का उद्देश्य चिकित्सा शिक्षा की गुणवत्ता से समझौता किए बिना नियामक प्रक्रियाओं को सरल बनाना और ओवरलैपिंग जिम्मेदारियों को खत्म करना है।)

• 1. Core Context & Background: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges. Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk. The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules. Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open. The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015. In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”. For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia. Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Weekend / gaming and lottery / lifestyle and leisure / technology (general) / games / leisure (general)

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 03:21:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open. The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015. In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”. For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia. Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Weekend / gaming and lottery / lifestyle and leisure / technology (general) / games / leisure (general)

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Core accountability: On core sector performance' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

The author contends that 'Core accountability: On core sector performan' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth.

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.question: Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Core accountability: On core sector performance"?

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite...
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.hinglishExplanation: Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite..." (Hinglish Arth: यदि यह भूमिगत संसाधनों की कमी का मामला है, तो यह एक बात है, लेकिन तेल और गैस सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रमों का खराब प्रदर्शन बिल्कुल अलग है।)

hinglishTracks.en: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — यहां तक ​​कि कम आधार प्रभाव भी भारत के तेल और गैस क्षेत्रों को विकास में नहीं धकेल सका।

hinglishTracks.en: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अक्टूबर में मुख्य क्षेत्र का प्रदर्शन इस बात का अच्छा उदाहरण है कि कैसे सांख्यिकीय विकृतियाँ अर्थव्यवस्था का गलत आकलन कर सकती हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — 10.9% की विकास दर, जो एक श्रृंखला की उच्चतम दर है, को भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की ताकत और लचीलेपन के संकेत के रूप में मनाया गया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Resilience' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: लचीलापन और मज़बूती — किसी बड़े संकट या मंदी के बाद तेज़ी से वापस उभरने की क्षमता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Robustness, Endurance, Adaptability और Antonyms हैं: Fragility, Vulnerability, Weakness।

hinglishTracks.en: There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं है, इसका एक पहलू संख्याओं में परिलक्षित हुआ है, विशेषकर बुनियादी ढांचे के निर्माण से संबंधित है।।

hinglishTracks.en: However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — हालाँकि, उच्च कोर सेक्टर की वृद्धि के पीछे अधिक प्रभावशाली कारक कम आधार प्रभाव था।।

hinglishTracks.en: The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — अक्टूबर 2025 में कोर इंडस्ट्रीज का समग्र सूचकांक केवल 0.8% बढ़ा और इसलिए, इसके संबंध में, अक्टूबर 2026 में प्रदर्शन इतना तेज दिख रहा था।।

hinglishTracks.en: This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — सूचकांक के भीतर अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों को देखने पर यह निम्न आधार प्रभाव और भी स्पष्ट होता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — कोयला क्षेत्र अक्टूबर में 23% की तेज़ गति से बढ़ा, जो पिछले महीने की वृद्धि दर से दोगुने से भी अधिक है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — फिर भी, इसका एक बड़ा हिस्सा इस तथ्य से प्रेरित था कि इस क्षेत्र में पिछले अक्टूबर में लगभग 8.5% की गिरावट आई थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — डेटा से पता चलता है कि बाकी क्षेत्र की वृद्धि बिजली और लौह अयस्क क्षेत्रों की मांग से प्रेरित थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — बिजली क्षेत्र भी अक्टूबर में लगभग 22% की उच्च दर पर बढ़ा, लेकिन पिछले साल अक्टूबर में लगभग 7% संकुचन के कारण।।

hinglishTracks.en: This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यह आधार प्रभाव विसंगति संभवतः इस तथ्य के कारण है कि त्योहारी सीज़न हर साल अलग-अलग लेकिन समान बिंदुओं पर शुरू होता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ऐसे में, नवंबर के आंकड़े उपलब्ध होने के बाद अर्थव्यवस्था की अधिक सटीक रीडिंग संभव हो सकेगी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — ऐसा प्रतीत होता है कि निर्माण-संबंधित क्षेत्रों में वास्तविक वृद्धि देखी गई है, जो सरकार के चल रहे बुनियादी ढांचे के प्रयास का प्रतिबिंब है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — लौह अयस्क क्षेत्र की विकास दर अक्टूबर 2026 में तीन महीने के उच्चतम स्तर 26.4% पर पहुंच गई, जबकि पिछले साल इसी महीने में 8.7% की वृद्धि हुई थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — स्टील में पिछले वर्ष 9.5% के मुकाबले 7.3% और सीमेंट में 5.2% के मुकाबले 15.4% की वृद्धि हुई।।

hinglishTracks.en: The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — निकट भविष्य में सरकारी खर्च पर अर्थव्यवस्था की निर्भरता कम होने वाली नहीं है, और यह और भी बढ़ सकती है क्योंकि ऊंची लागत कंपनियों के लाभ मार्जिन को प्रभावित कर रही है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — कोर सेक्टर डेटा ने एक बार फिर इन उच्च लागतों का एक प्रमुख कारण उजागर किया - तेल और गैस क्षेत्र।।

hinglishTracks.en: The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — कच्चे तेल क्षेत्र में 4.1% की गिरावट आई, यह संकुचन का लगातार 22वां महीना है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — इसी तरह, प्राकृतिक गैस क्षेत्र में 7.6% की गिरावट आई, जो श्रृंखला का सबसे खराब प्रदर्शन और संकुचन का लगातार 28वां महीना है।।

hinglishTracks.en: A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — भारत में उच्च मुद्रास्फीति के पीछे एक प्रमुख कारण इन दोनों क्षेत्रों का खराब प्रदर्शन और इसके परिणामस्वरूप आयातित ईंधन पर निर्भरता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Inflation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महंगाई (मुद्रास्फीति) — जब बाज़ार में वस्तुओं के दाम बढ़ें और रुपये की खरीद शक्ति कम हो जाए। इसके Synonyms हैं: Price-escalation, Hyperinflation, Dearness और Antonyms हैं: Deflation, Disinflation, Recession।

hinglishTracks.en: It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अब समय आ गया है कि पेट्रोलियम मंत्रालय स्पष्ट रूप से बताए - दिसंबर में संसद को या सीधे जनता को - क्यों भारत का ईंधन उत्पादन लगातार गिर रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.en: If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — यदि यह भूमिगत संसाधनों की कमी का मामला है, तो यह एक बात है, लेकिन तेल और गैस सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रमों का खराब प्रदर्शन बिल्कुल अलग है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Underperformance' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Underperformance' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: Accountability needs to be set.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — जवाबदेही तय करने की जरूरत है.। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Accountability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability और Antonyms हैं: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility।
