🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:58:17 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Children who lived in Brazilian neighbourhoods buzzing with a special kind of mosquito were far less likely to catch dengue or another worrisome virus, chikungunya, researchers reported Saturday. The major study of more than 5,700 children in one of the world's dengue hot spots offers new evidence that breeding mosquitoes unable to transmit these viruses can be a viable strategy rather than solely relying on pesticides and trying to avoid getting bitten. In neighbourhoods populated by these so-called Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, researchers found about a 69% reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections in schoolchildren compared to similar neighbourhoods — an effect sustained even during Brazil's severe 2024 dengue outbreak, said Dr. Sri Edupuganti of Emory University, part of the international research team. The researchers reported the findings at a meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. “This is really exciting,” said David Hamer, a global health expert at Boston University who wasn't involved with the Brazilian study. He predicts that pairing more use of these Wolbachia mosquitoes with existing steps to fight mosquito-borne disease could “knock dengue down to much lower levels” in many places. The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s. Usually in the continental US, dengue is found mostly in people who travelled internationally. But as of Friday, Florida health officials had tallied more than 650 locally acquired cases, about three-quarters of them in Hillsborough County, home to Tampa. Outside the U.S., the nonprofit World Mosquito Program has pioneered the Wolbachia strategy. How it works: Scientists breed mosquitoes to carry a kind of bacteria called Wolbachia. It is harmless to people and common in many insects, although not dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacteria dramatically reduce the mosquitoes' ability to transmit certain viruses. Female mosquitoes spread the bacteria to their offspring, so releasing enough of the specially bred insects — males and females — into an area allows Wolbachia to gradually become established in the local mosquito population.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Field trials and other studies in Indonesia and elsewhere have shown the strategy can significantly lower dengue diagnoses. But because people with mild symptoms may not be diagnosed, the new study in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, went further. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Predictably (Adverb)
जैसा पहले से अनुमान था — बिना किसी आश्चर्य के बिल्कुल पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक होना।
✓ Syn: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably  |  ✖ Ant: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Continental (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Continental' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Scientists report strong new evidence that speci' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Scientists report strong new evidence that sp' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Scientists report strong new evidence that sp' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S." (Hinglish Arth: नवीनतम शोध तब आया है जब फ्लोरिडा असामान्य रूप से बड़े पैमाने पर वायरस के प्रकोप से जूझ रहा है, जो किसी भी यू.एस. में सबसे बड़ा प्रतीत होता है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus." (Hinglish Arth: शोधकर्ताओं ने डेंगू, चिकनगुनिया या जीका वायरस के लक्षणों के लिए रक्त का परीक्षण किया।)

articles.title: No cluster kitchens for midday meals in Karnataka, says Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Minister says that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has assured that cluster kitchens (centralised cooking facilities) will not be established under the scheme providing midday meals to schoolchildren (Classes I to X) in the State. He said that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs. On Monday, S. Balan, honorary president of Akshara Dasoha (Midday Meal Workers’ Union), met the Minister at his residence and submitted a list of demands, including not entertaining the idea of cluster kitchens. The delegation also sought a hike in monthly remuneration, citing the example of Keralam, where workers are paid ₹12,000, compared with ₹4,600 to ₹4,700 in Karnataka. Mr. Bangarappa said he would discuss the demand with the Chief Minister. “It is to our government’s credit that we previously raised the retirement corpus for midday meal workers to ₹40,000,” he said. He advised the union to meet Union government officials, noting that the midday meal scheme is not solely funded by the State government and involves participation from the Centre as well. Mr. Balan also raised concerns over substandard grains and rice being supplied to government schools to cook midday meals for children. The Minister sought precise details on where such incidents were occurring, promising strict action.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister outlining various demands, including the establishment of joint bank accounts for school headmasters and head cooks, a retirement corpus of at least ₹1 lakh, and a monthly pension of ₹5,000.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 No cluster kitchens for midday meals in Karnataka, says Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:25:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Minister says that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has assured that cluster kitchens (centralised cooking facilities) will not be established under the scheme providing midday meals to schoolchildren (Classes I to X) in the State. He said that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs. On Monday, S. Balan, honorary president of Akshara Dasoha (Midday Meal Workers’ Union), met the Minister at his residence and submitted a list of demands, including not entertaining the idea of cluster kitchens. The delegation also sought a hike in monthly remuneration, citing the example of Keralam, where workers are paid ₹12,000, compared with ₹4,600 to ₹4,700 in Karnataka. Mr. Bangarappa said he would discuss the demand with the Chief Minister. “It is to our government’s credit that we previously raised the retirement corpus for midday meal workers to ₹40,000,” he said. He advised the union to meet Union government officials, noting that the midday meal scheme is not solely funded by the State government and involves participation from the Centre as well. Mr. Balan also raised concerns over substandard grains and rice being supplied to government schools to cook midday meals for children. The Minister sought precise details on where such incidents were occurring, promising strict action.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister outlining various demands, including the establishment of joint bank accounts for school headmasters and head cooks, a retirement corpus of at least ₹1 lakh, and a monthly pension of ₹5,000.

जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।

Establishment (Adjective)
स्थापना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Establishment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Remuneration (Noun)
पारिश्रमिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Remuneration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 was exposed on ECI citizen service portal, claims report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For at least three years, the personal data that voters submitted to the Election Commission of India through Form 6, the application for registration as an elector, was exposed on its Citizen Service Portal (https://voters.eci.gov.in/ ) to anyone with a login, claims a report by ‘Charchagram’, a civic-tech initiative for building tools for enhancing transparency and accountability in public systems of India. It said that while records going back to 2023 were verified for this report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer. According to the report, using ECI published data, it estimates that at least seven crore Form 6 enrolments took place in this period. Each Form 6 application holds a citizen’s name, their relative’s name, gender, phone number, email, home address, photograph, Aadhaar details, age-proof documents, and address-proof documents, among other details. “We audited the front-end code available in public. And while auditing, [we] found that there is URL through which anyone can access Form 6 data of other voters,” said Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at Charchagram. Opening “voters.eci.gov.in/form6?refId= ” returned a web-page showing all the applicants’ details to any logged-in user, regardless of who the applicant was. “The reference IDs follow a predictable state, constituency, type and date/sequence pattern. The server did not check that the application belonged to the person asking. The predictability of the reference ID amplifies this security issue, since any user can scrape the data one by one in large volumes,” according to the report. Following the revelation, Charchagram says it reported the matter privately to the ECI and to CERT-In. CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents as and when they occur.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr. Rajput said.

And while auditing, [we] found that there is URL through which anyone can access Form 6 data of other voters,” said Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at Charchagram. Opening “voters.eci.gov.in/form6?refId= ” returned a web-page showing all the applicants’ details to any logged-in user, regardless of who the applicant was. “The reference IDs follow a predictable state, constituency, type and date/sequence pattern. The server did not check that the application belonged to the person asking. The predictability of the reference ID amplifies this security issue, since any user can scrape the data one by one in large volumes,” according to the report. Following the revelation, Charchagram says it reported the matter privately to the ECI and to CERT-In. CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents as and when they occur.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr. Rajput said.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For at least three years, the personal data that voters submitted to the Election Commission of India through Form 6, the application for registration as an elector, was exposed on its Citizen Service Portal (https://voters.eci.gov.in/ ) to anyone with a login, claims a report by ‘Charchagram’, a civic-tech initiative for building tools for enhancing transparency and accountability in public systems of India. It said that while records going back to 2023 were verified for this report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer. According to the report, using ECI published data, it estimates that at least seven crore Form 6 enrolments took place in this period. Each Form 6 application holds a citizen’s name, their relative’s name, gender, phone number, email, home address, photograph, Aadhaar details, age-proof documents, and address-proof documents, among other details. “We audited the front-end code available in public. And while auditing, [we] found that there is URL through which anyone can access Form 6 data of other voters,” said Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at Charchagram. Opening “voters.eci.gov.in/form6?refId= ” returned a web-page showing all the applicants’ details to any logged-in user, regardless of who the applicant was. “The reference IDs follow a predictable state, constituency, type and date/sequence pattern. The server did not check that the application belonged to the person asking. The predictability of the reference ID amplifies this security issue, since any user can scrape the data one by one in large volumes,” according to the report. Following the revelation, Charchagram says it reported the matter privately to the ECI and to CERT-In. CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents as and when they occur.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr. Rajput said.

articles.title: A.P. CM calls for wider use of AI in healthcare, agriculture to improve public services
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Chandrababu Naidu directs senior officials to take up capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has called for the wider application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across various sectors, including healthcare and agriculture, to improve service delivery, administrative efficiency and government revenue. Reviewing the functioning of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) with senior officials of various departments on Sunday, Mr. Naidu stressed the need to leverage modern technology and the AI stack to simplify government services and improve the performance of departments. He directed officials to take measures to ensure that public services were delivered more efficiently and promptly. He also called for capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees. Stressing that delays in addressing public grievances should be avoided, the Chief Minister has directed officials to expedite the resolution of complaints received through the Public Grievance Redressal System. A positive public perception of government services was essential for improving governance and called upon departments to regularly review their performance and address shortcomings in monitoring mechanisms, he said. Mr. Naidu said the government was using Revenue and Legal AI stacks to analyse various issues and identify ways to improve departmental performance. Data-driven decision-making would become increasingly important in governance in the coming years, he observed. Referring to the recent local body elections, he said the results could serve as one of the indicators of the government’s performance. He asked senior departmental officials to strengthen monitoring mechanisms and ensure better delivery of services to the public.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior officials from the Social Welfare, BC Welfare, Minority Welfare, Finance, Municipal Administration and Energy departments, besides RTGS officials, participated in the review meeting.

Data-driven decision-making would become increasingly important in governance in the coming years, he observed. Referring to the recent local body elections, he said the results could serve as one of the indicators of the government’s performance. He asked senior departmental officials to strengthen monitoring mechanisms and ensure better delivery of services to the public.

articles.title: Government will explore all possible ways to avoid electricity restriction in Keralam, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Sunny Joseph announces that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government will explore all possible ways to avoid power restrictions in the State, Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph has said. Addressing a Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) review meeting at Thodupuzha in Idukki on Monday, Joseph said that due to the El Niño effect, rainfall has been largely reduced in the State, affecting the storage levels of hydroelectric dams. “Compared to the previous year, the water level in Idukki, including major hydel dams, is more than 20% below storage this year. Presently, there is only 60% storage in the hydel dams in the State,” the Minister said. Mr. Joseph further noted that the government will t launch initiatives to arrange power from other sources. According to KSEB data, the water level in the Idukki dam on Monday was 2,368.9 feet (63%), compared with 2,384.98 feet (79%) on the same day last year. During the meeting, the Minister announced that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1. He said the decision was taken based on repeated demands from various quarters. The Minister also directed officials to take steps to resume the boating facility at the Anayirankal dam reservoir. Based on the recommendation of a panel appointed by the High Court to address human-animal conflicts in Chinnakkanal, the boating facility in Anayirankal was suspended following the court’s direction on July 14, 2023. The panel had argued that stopping the boating facility in Anayirankal would help prevent human-elephant conflicts in the Anayirankal and Chinnakkanal regions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Joseph further noted that to tap the tourism potential in Idukki, the KSEB and the Tourism department will jointly implement projects in the district. He also said the Electricity department will seek permission from the forest department to set up an overhead power line to Edamalakkudy, the State’s first tribal panchayat, to provide electricity to the tribal community.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Government will explore all possible ways to avoid electricity restriction in Keralam, says Minister

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:19:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Sunny Joseph announces that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government will explore all possible ways to avoid power restrictions in the State, Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph has said. Addressing a Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) review meeting at Thodupuzha in Idukki on Monday, Joseph said that due to the El Niño effect, rainfall has been largely reduced in the State, affecting the storage levels of hydroelectric dams. “Compared to the previous year, the water level in Idukki, including major hydel dams, is more than 20% below storage this year. Presently, there is only 60% storage in the hydel dams in the State,” the Minister said. Mr. Joseph further noted that the government will t launch initiatives to arrange power from other sources. According to KSEB data, the water level in the Idukki dam on Monday was 2,368.9 feet (63%), compared with 2,384.98 feet (79%) on the same day last year. During the meeting, the Minister announced that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1. He said the decision was taken based on repeated demands from various quarters. The Minister also directed officials to take steps to resume the boating facility at the Anayirankal dam reservoir. Based on the recommendation of a panel appointed by the High Court to address human-animal conflicts in Chinnakkanal, the boating facility in Anayirankal was suspended following the court’s direction on July 14, 2023. The panel had argued that stopping the boating facility in Anayirankal would help prevent human-elephant conflicts in the Anayirankal and Chinnakkanal regions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Joseph further noted that to tap the tourism potential in Idukki, the KSEB and the Tourism department will jointly implement projects in the district. He also said the Electricity department will seek permission from the forest department to set up an overhead power line to Edamalakkudy, the State’s first tribal panchayat, to provide electricity to the tribal community.

articles.title: Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: B.Y. Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process. He expressed hope that the airport would become active again, with several flights operating from there.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking to presspersons in Shivamogga on Monday, Mr. Raghavendra said uncertainty over the airport’s inclusion had persisted for the past 15 to 20 days, and that it now appeared to be clearing. The last date for bids is December 31. He said that under the earlier version of the scheme, an airport would have a one-year commercial break after three years of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support for flight operations. This time, following requests from people’s representatives, including himself, the Centre has included the airport in the next tender without any such break. He said this would allow Shivamogga to grow commercially under UDAN over the next five years, and that flight services would follow naturally. Unlike earlier tenders, the current one does not name specific routes. Airlines have the freedom to choose which routes to operate from Shivamogga, and bidders would be eligible for UDAN subsidy. Mr. Raghavendra said efforts were under way to hold talks with three airlines about their participation in the tender. He thanked the Prime Minister, former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa and Union Minister Pralhad Joshi for their support. Mr. Raghavendra said the tender process could take until February or March 2027 to be finalised and for operations to begin, which could leave a gap of three to four months. He urged the State government to provide temporary VGF support for two to three months in the interim, at least for the Shivamogga–Bengaluru and Shivamogga–Hyderabad routes, or one of them. If an airline chose these routes under the tender, he said, the State could withdraw its support. Regarding cargo services and night landing, he said decisions would be taken after a survey based on local demand, crops and export opportunities was conducted.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Flight operations under UDAN from Shivamogga airport ended last week. As a result, the airport built at Sogane, near Shivamogga, has gone silent. It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:19:10 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: B.Y. Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process. He expressed hope that the airport would become active again, with several flights operating from there.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking to presspersons in Shivamogga on Monday, Mr. Raghavendra said uncertainty over the airport’s inclusion had persisted for the past 15 to 20 days, and that it now appeared to be clearing. The last date for bids is December 31. He said that under the earlier version of the scheme, an airport would have a one-year commercial break after three years of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support for flight operations. This time, following requests from people’s representatives, including himself, the Centre has included the airport in the next tender without any such break. He said this would allow Shivamogga to grow commercially under UDAN over the next five years, and that flight services would follow naturally. Unlike earlier tenders, the current one does not name specific routes. Airlines have the freedom to choose which routes to operate from Shivamogga, and bidders would be eligible for UDAN subsidy. Mr. Raghavendra said efforts were under way to hold talks with three airlines about their participation in the tender. He thanked the Prime Minister, former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa and Union Minister Pralhad Joshi for their support. Mr. Raghavendra said the tender process could take until February or March 2027 to be finalised and for operations to begin, which could leave a gap of three to four months. He urged the State government to provide temporary VGF support for two to three months in the interim, at least for the Shivamogga–Bengaluru and Shivamogga–Hyderabad routes, or one of them. If an airline chose these routes under the tender, he said, the State could withdraw its support. Regarding cargo services and night landing, he said decisions would be taken after a survey based on local demand, crops and export opportunities was conducted.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Flight operations under UDAN from Shivamogga airport ended last week. As a result, the airport built at Sogane, near Shivamogga, has gone silent. It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Inclusive (Adjective)
समावेशी — जिसमें समाज के हर वर्ग (खासकर गरीब और वंचित वर्ग) को बराबर शामिल किया जाए।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Egalitarian, All-encompassing  |  ✖ Ant: Exclusive, Discriminatory, Narrow
Participation (Noun)
भाग लेना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Participation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Commercial (Adjective)
व्यावसायिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Commercial' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Viability (Noun)
व्यवहार्यता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Viability' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender p' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tende' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tende' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process." (Hinglish Arth: शिवमोग्गा के सांसद राघवेंद्र ने कहा कि केंद्र सरकार ने शिवमोग्गा हवाई अड्डे को संशोधित UDAN 6.0 निविदा प्रक्रिया में शामिल करने का निर्णय लिया है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023." (Hinglish Arth: इसका उद्घाटन फरवरी 2023 में हुआ था और यह अगस्त 2023 से संचालित हो रहा है।)

articles.title: 3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The three-member committee of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) which met here on Monday to discuss the drinking water needs of the two member States — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — for the next three months ended without taking any decision as Telangana strongly opposed A.P.’s indent of 19 tmc ft water, including 10 tmc ft for Krishna Delta System from Nagarjunasagar dam. The meeting chaired by Member-Secretary of the river board Satish Kumar Kamboj was attended by Engineers-in-Chief of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh O.V. Ramesh Babu and K. Narasimha Murthy. The meeting prolonged from forenoon to evening but no decision was taken as there was no consensus on utilisation of water available in Nagarjunsagar reservoir. In addition to the water indent placed by A.P. before the meeting for release of 9 tmc ft water from NS Right Canal, they also sought another 10 tmc ft water release from the reservoir for meeting the needs in the Krishna Delta System (KDS). On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar. Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir. He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema. There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar. Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir. He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema. There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:16:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The three-member committee of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) which met here on Monday to discuss the drinking water needs of the two member States — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — for the next three months ended without taking any decision as Telangana strongly opposed A.P.’s indent of 19 tmc ft water, including 10 tmc ft for Krishna Delta System from Nagarjunasagar dam. The meeting chaired by Member-Secretary of the river board Satish Kumar Kamboj was attended by Engineers-in-Chief of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh O.V. Ramesh Babu and K. Narasimha Murthy. The meeting prolonged from forenoon to evening but no decision was taken as there was no consensus on utilisation of water available in Nagarjunsagar reservoir. In addition to the water indent placed by A.P. before the meeting for release of 9 tmc ft water from NS Right Canal, they also sought another 10 tmc ft water release from the reservoir for meeting the needs in the Krishna Delta System (KDS). On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar. Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir. He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema. There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025. Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%. These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks. The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements. The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance. SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / business (general) / banking / Reserve Bank of India / financial and business service

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #15 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:16:07 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025. Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%. These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks. The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements. The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance. SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / business (general) / banking / Reserve Bank of India / financial and business service

✓ Syn: Robustness, Endurance, Adaptability  |  ✖ Ant: Fragility, Vulnerability, Weakness
Classification (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Classification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Conservation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

articles.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance. Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. "We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said. "We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner." European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks. Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries. He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies. "NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering. A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 06:57:46 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance. Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. "We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said. "We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner." European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks. Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries. He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies. "NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering. A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

अभिनव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Innovative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur. Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees. Regular weekly services will begin on November 28. Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’. Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said. Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship. It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations. Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi. Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Nepal PM India visit LIVE: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 06:40:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur. Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees. Regular weekly services will begin on November 28. Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’. Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said. Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship. It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations. Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi. Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.

articles.title: Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay. Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart. The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings. Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs. Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand. “Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said. The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest. A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions. There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives. Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay. Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart. The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings. Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs. Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand. “Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said. The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest. A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions. There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives. Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended setting up a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, contending that China may turn the process into an international contest over legitimacy. A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in a report to the U.S. Congress, made a strong pitch to recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole legitimate authority to identify and recognise the successor to the 14th Dalai Lama. The report by the bipartisan Commission said China was likely to use coercive tools to shape the outcome of the succession process. It said that the U.S. Congress should adopt a policy of not recognising any successor to the Dalai Lama who is selected or installed by China. “To carry out this policy and ensure U.S. government readiness for the Dalai Lama’s succession, Congress should direct the Secretary of State to… establish a senior-level channel with the Government of India for succession contingency planning, including intelligence sharing on Chinese influence operations,” the report said. It also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to lead an internal interagency tabletop exercise on succession scenarios, with participation by the National Security Advisor, the Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defence. The commission also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to conduct Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues and tabletop exercises with Indian counterparts on the political and security implications of succession scenarios. The Commission also wanted the U.S. to coordinate with allies and partners on a diplomatic response that denies international legitimacy to any successor selected by China.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It also wanted the U.S. to counter succession-related influence operations by strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration’s cybersecurity and resilience against China’s cyber and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled disinformation campaigns.

1. Core Context & Background: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended setting up a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, contending that China may turn the process into an international contest over legitimacy. A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in a report to the U.S. Congress, made a strong pitch to recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole legitimate authority to identify and recognise the successor to the 14th Dalai Lama. The report by the bipartisan Commission said China was likely to use coercive tools to shape the outcome of the succession process. It said that the U.S. Congress should adopt a policy of not recognising any successor to the Dalai Lama who is selected or installed by China. “To carry out this policy and ensure U.S. government readiness for the Dalai Lama’s succession, Congress should direct the Secretary of State to… establish a senior-level channel with the Government of India for succession contingency planning, including intelligence sharing on Chinese influence operations,” the report said. It also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to lead an internal interagency tabletop exercise on succession scenarios, with participation by the National Security Advisor, the Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defence. The commission also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to conduct Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues and tabletop exercises with Indian counterparts on the political and security implications of succession scenarios. The Commission also wanted the U.S. to coordinate with allies and partners on a diplomatic response that denies international legitimacy to any successor selected by China.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It also wanted the U.S. to counter succession-related influence operations by strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration’s cybersecurity and resilience against China’s cyber and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled disinformation campaigns.

articles.title: China says ready to work with India to facilitate visa issuance for business people
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals. "China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said in a written reply to questions by PTI about the reported reductions in visa issuance for Indians. “We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said. The spokesperson's remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas. Also, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly given visas to attend this month’s China Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair attracts businessmen from around the world to showcase their businesses to Chinese consumers. Beijing has also stopped the service provider China Visa Application Centre from accepting visa applications, and its missions have begun handling them directly amid rising demand for Chinese visas, especially business visas. The visa process between the two countries improved after India began issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years, amid efforts to repair bilateral ties that came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020. The resumption of the visas was regarded as a significant move as the two countries started the normalisation process after a freeze in bilateral ties. With liberalised visa processes, the two countries launched direct air services connecting several cities, including Beijing-New Delhi.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has been reduced to around 7% in recent months to encourage more business and tourism-related travel to India.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 China says ready to work with India to facilitate visa issuance for business people

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 04:25:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals. "China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said in a written reply to questions by PTI about the reported reductions in visa issuance for Indians. “We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said. The spokesperson's remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas. Also, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly given visas to attend this month’s China Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair attracts businessmen from around the world to showcase their businesses to Chinese consumers. Beijing has also stopped the service provider China Visa Application Centre from accepting visa applications, and its missions have begun handling them directly amid rising demand for Chinese visas, especially business visas. The visa process between the two countries improved after India began issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years, amid efforts to repair bilateral ties that came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020. The resumption of the visas was regarded as a significant move as the two countries started the normalisation process after a freeze in bilateral ties. With liberalised visa processes, the two countries launched direct air services connecting several cities, including Beijing-New Delhi.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has been reduced to around 7% in recent months to encourage more business and tourism-related travel to India.

articles.title: Study finds PTSD-specific brain changes, paving way for personalised treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD. Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a mental health disorder in which one experiences flashbacks or nightmares of a terrifying or life-threatening event. The study, published in the journal ' Cell Reports' , also found that among people affected by PTSD, the molecular variations appeared to be driven by a number of factors, including the sex and race of the person, and whether the trauma exposure occurred in childhood or adulthood. "The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said. "The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said. The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said. A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder. Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory. The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Study finds PTSD-specific brain changes, paving way for personalised treatment

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:36:22 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD. Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a mental health disorder in which one experiences flashbacks or nightmares of a terrifying or life-threatening event. The study, published in the journal ' Cell Reports' , also found that among people affected by PTSD, the molecular variations appeared to be driven by a number of factors, including the sex and race of the person, and whether the trauma exposure occurred in childhood or adulthood. "The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said. "The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said. The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said. A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder. Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory. The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

"The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said. "The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said. The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said. A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder. Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory. The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

articles.title: Many children may be wearing spectacles with the wrong prescription. What does this mean for their vision?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The objective is not merely to ensure that children wear spectacles, but that the prescription is appropriate, the lenses are correctly dispensed and their vision is monitored as they grow

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An incorrect or outdated spectacles prescription can leave a child’s vision inadequately corrected, affecting classroom activities and learning. Regular eye examinations are important because children’s eyesight can change as they grow, and wearing spectacles alone does not ensure that their vision is being corrected properly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A study of 5,268 school-going children in north India found that only 23.03% of those prescribed spectacles were using the correct prescription. Inaccurate spectacle power was common, with younger age and longer duration of spectacle use among the associated factors.

articles.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing. The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), a laser procedure used to correct vision. At six hours after surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving a placebo. Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases. The company said there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial. Shares of the eye-care company fell 1.4% in extended trading.
