articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

articles.title: Ex-U.K. PM Theresa May tells successor to ‘move on’ from Brexit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Former British Prime Minister Theresa May said she was “aghast” that Prime Minister Andy Burnham could be considering rejoining the European Union, after he sealed trade and youth mobility deals in Brussels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ms. May’s remarks came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials on Friday (November 20, 2026) sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility. A decade after Britain narrowly voted to leave the bloc, Mr. Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties ahead of a government 10-year plan for the U.K., set to be unveiled next month. Ms. May warned that negotiations with the EU risked taking up vast amounts of government time, hampering efforts to tackle other issues. “And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU,” she said. Ms. May, who supported remaining in the 27-member bloc, said government had to respect the result of the 2016 referendum. “When I became prime minister, I was very clear. People have voted for Brexit. We should deliver Brexit,” she told BBC television. “He (Burnham) wants to pat them (voters) on their head and say ‘you know what? Remember that vote? Well you got it wrong, didn’t you? So have another go and come up with the right answer’,” she said. Ms. May was forced to quit in May 2019 after failing to get her Brexit deal through parliament. “My message to him (Burnham) really is: People voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on,” she added. Mr. Burnham, who has been in office since July 2026, has committed to his predecessor Keir Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement. But pro-Brexit campaigners fear he will push at some point to rejoin the 27-nation grouping. Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”. “That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”. “We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Ex-U.K. PM Theresa May tells successor to ‘move on’ from Brexit

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:00:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Former British Prime Minister Theresa May said she was “aghast” that Prime Minister Andy Burnham could be considering rejoining the European Union, after he sealed trade and youth mobility deals in Brussels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ms. May’s remarks came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials on Friday (November 20, 2026) sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility. A decade after Britain narrowly voted to leave the bloc, Mr. Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties ahead of a government 10-year plan for the U.K., set to be unveiled next month. Ms. May warned that negotiations with the EU risked taking up vast amounts of government time, hampering efforts to tackle other issues. “And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU,” she said. Ms. May, who supported remaining in the 27-member bloc, said government had to respect the result of the 2016 referendum. “When I became prime minister, I was very clear. People have voted for Brexit. We should deliver Brexit,” she told BBC television. “He (Burnham) wants to pat them (voters) on their head and say ‘you know what? Remember that vote? Well you got it wrong, didn’t you? So have another go and come up with the right answer’,” she said. Ms. May was forced to quit in May 2019 after failing to get her Brexit deal through parliament. “My message to him (Burnham) really is: People voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on,” she added. Mr. Burnham, who has been in office since July 2026, has committed to his predecessor Keir Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement. But pro-Brexit campaigners fear he will push at some point to rejoin the 27-nation grouping. Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”. “That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”. “We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies. Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026). A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”. On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu. 🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:58:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies. Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026). A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”. On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu. Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting the outgoing Prime Minister and his government. It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people”, without the participation of Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to his remaining in power.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

articles.title: Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company. Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported. The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang. Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully. Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure. The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:37:04 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company. Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported. The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang. Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully. Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure. The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company. Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported. The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang. Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully. Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure. The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — अनुसंधान संस्थानों को समय पर वित्त पोषण, बेहतर शिक्षण प्रोत्साहन, अधिक स्वायत्तता, नेतृत्व नियंत्रण, बदले की भावना के खिलाफ सुरक्षा उपाय और कम प्रशासनिक बोझ की आवश्यकता है। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — आधुनिक विज्ञान उचित ही स्वतंत्र जांच पर गर्व करता है, चाहे जांचकर्ता कहीं भी स्थित हो।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Irrespective' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Irrespective' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ऐसा कोई कारण नहीं है कि भारत के बाहर के किसी व्यक्ति का मूल्यांकन उपनिवेशवाद माना जाए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — फिर भी प्रधान मंत्री की आर्थिक सलाहकार परिषद में क्रमशः सदस्य, संयुक्त निदेशक और एक युवा पेशेवर, संजीव सान्याल, सात्विक देव और पायल शर्मा द्वारा व्यापक रूप से बहस किए गए लेख में यह आरोप लगाया गया था।।

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / France / space programme / defence equipment / Artificial Intelligence / economy / security measures / United Nations / technology (general) / oceans / climate change / ISRO / water / summit / weather science / science (general) / law

hinglishTracks.en: India and France are charting a shared space future
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — भारत और फ्रांस साझा अंतरिक्ष भविष्य की योजना बना रहे हैं।

hinglishTracks.en: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — 60 से अधिक वर्षों से, फ्रांस और भारत ने दुनिया में सबसे लंबे समय से चली आ रही और सबसे भरोसेमंद अंतरिक्ष साझेदारियों में से एक को साझा किया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ऐसे समय में जब अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वातावरण तेजी से जटिल हो गया है, यह साझेदारी पहले से कहीं अधिक मायने रखती है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

hinglishTracks.en: Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — 1998 के बाद से, उनकी रणनीतिक साझेदारी रक्षा सहयोग पर निर्भर रही है - अलौएट III/चेतक और राफेल विमान से लेकर भारत में निर्मित स्कॉर्पीन पनडुब्बियों तक - और लोगों से लोगों के बीच संबंध, समय के साथ विस्तारित होकर इसमें कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता, नीली अर्थव्यवस्था और बहुत कुछ शामिल है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Intelligence' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Intelligence' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उनकी विशेष वैश्विक रणनीतिक साझेदारी के बारे में उल्लेखनीय बात यह है कि, उनके राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा सिद्धांत के मूल में, वे दोनों रणनीतिक स्वायत्तता की अवधारणा साझा करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — रणनीतिक स्वायत्तता का मतलब स्वयं को साझेदारों से अलग करना नहीं है।।

hinglishTracks.en: France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

articles.title: Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

hinglishTracks.en: The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:15:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Conservative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Achievement (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Achievement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Progressive (Adjective)
प्रगतिशील — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Progressive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine." (Hinglish Arth: कादम्बिनी गांगुली ने बाधाओं को तोड़ते हुए पश्चिमी चिकित्सा का अभ्यास करने वाली भारत की पहली महिला चिकित्सकों में से एक बन गईं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades." (Hinglish Arth: चिकित्सा और सामाजिक क्षेत्र में उनके योगदान को पूर्ण मान्यता बहुत बाद में, हाल के दशकों में ही मिली।)

articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

📰 Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:50:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: climate change / Turkey / politics / Australia / electricity production and distribution / energy and resource / European Union / solar / India / China / carbon emissions / population / economy / carbon capture and sequestration / Artificial Intelligence / data management storage

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: international court or tribunal / Myanmar / Rohingya crisis / crime / armed Forces / sexual assault / Bangladesh / Citizenship / welfare / United Nations / China / Russia / India / democracy

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

1. Core Context & Background: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

The Hingalganj MLA was taken off ventilator support on Monday (November 23, 2026) and has not required it since. She is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly, BJP leader Archana Das Majumdar said. However, the three-member medical team treating her is not willing to take any chances and has recommended that she remain in the ICU for continued monitoring. Hospital sources said she was still receiving supplemental oxygen due to low oxygen levels in her body. While other clinical parameters indicate a positive recovery, doctors remain concerned about possible complications arising from the poisoning. Following the suspected poisoning, excessive saliva had accumulated in Ms. Patra's mouth. As she was not fully conscious, some saliva entered her lungs, affecting oxygen supply to the body, an earlier CT scan had found. Doctors said the effects of impaired oxygen supply to the lungs may not become immediately apparent and could manifest after some delay. A repeat CT scan of her chest was scheduled for Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon to assess the extent of any lung damage. Her further recovery would depend, among other factors, on the findings of the scan, they said. Meanwhile, doctors are yet to establish the exact composition of the suspected poison detected in her stomach.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the medical team, the substance found in her stomach was described as a herbal larvicide (herbal pesticide), but its precise ingredients remain unknown.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Intensifying the internal conflict within the Congress in Keralam, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on fellow party leader Shafi Parambil, MP, alleging that a coordinated cyber campaign was being orchestrated against him and warning that he would expose those behind it if the attacks continued. Challenging Mr. Parambil to an open public debate, Mr Unnithan said he was “ready to end his political career” if Mr Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless. He also claimed that he had recorded all relevant details in his personal diary and warned that the people involved, whom he described as “the teacher and the disciple”, would eventually be exposed. Mr Unnithan dismissed the claim that Mr. Parambil belonged to the ‘A’ group in the Congress, saying it would be “the eighth wonder of the world” to describe him as an A group leader. He clarified that he had not insulted Mr Parambil but had only stated that he did not belong to the group. Taking aim at those invoking the legacy of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, Mr Unnithan said many Congress leaders had stayed away when Chandy was being targeted, while others were concerned about protecting the public image. He questioned where those now speaking about the “Oommen Chandy school of politics” had been at the time. He also maintained that he had not received any personal benefits in Chandy’s name. Mr Unnithan alleged that the social media attacks against him were being conducted through fake accounts as part of a deliberate campaign rather than being spontaneous criticism. He claimed that the operation was being “controlled from Adoor and from a particular house.” Referring to a flat in Panampilly Nagar and a vehicle bearing the registration number 20-20, he hinted that he possessed information about those involved but declined to disclose further details immediately. “Everything is in my diary, the teacher and the disciple will both be trapped,” he warned, adding that he should not be unnecessarily provoked. He warned that if forced to reveal everything, “the respectable public image of certain people will be torn apart.” Mr Unnithan said he had always been “a lone fighter” within the party and had stood with former Congress leader K Karunakaran and Oommen Chandy “without expecting positions or personal gains.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Responding to allegations concerning his family, Mr Unnithan asserted that his son had never joined the BJP. Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed over to the BJP.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”. The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin. Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said. The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said. Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996. “This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal. VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD. The alliance had won 93 seats in the 1997 Assembly election, with the SAD winning 75 seats and the BJP winning 18 seats. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab’s trend of voting out incumbent governments.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SAD walked away from the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Badal also resigning her position as Minister in the Modi government at the Centre over the three farm laws that sought to re-engineer agri-commerce, igniting months-long protests on Delhi’s borders. 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Former Union Minister and BJP leader L. Murugan who was stopped by the police near the Annur bus stop in Coimbatore district, questioned the imposition of restrictions on his movement in Coimbatore district when the prohibitory orders were applicable to Madurai district. Speaking to reporters, Mr. Murugan said: “There is no relevance to the prohibitory orders imposed in Madurai to restrict movement in Coimbatore district. The police have not given me proper information or explained the reason for stopping me,” he said on Tuesday — T.C. Sibi Sreevathson Nainar Nagenthran, who left his home in Tirunelveli district at 2.35 pm for Thirupparankundram, was arrested at Thatchanallur check-post on Tirunelveli City outskirts at 3.15 pm along with a group of party functionaries. Police team led by Assistant Commissioner of Police, Palayamkottai, Rajamurali Ramachandran has been deployed in front of the house of Mr. Nagenthran to stop him from going to Thirupparankundram to participate in Karthigai Deepam festival. Here’s a look at the history and legal background of this long-running dispute. When a row broke out over lighting of Karthigai Deepam at the hill in Madurai, four Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniaswami Temple testified that the lamp had been lit at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since “time immemorial” The Bhattars conveyed this in a communication written to the temple authorities against the backdrop of a raging row over the Hindu Munnani’s demand for lighting the deepam at a different place. Explore the 30-year-old controversy over Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thirupparankundram, featuring testimonies from Sthaneeka Bhattars. In Thirupparankundram in Madurai, Hindus and Muslims live in camaraderie, but that has not kept the hill, which holds a couple of temples, a dargah, and some Jain beds, out of dispute. Here, we outline the history of judgments involving different petitioners through the years, in an attempt to understand the current crisis.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Explore the legal and political tensions in Thirupparankundram, where communal harmony faces challenges over religious practices and land disputes.
